patch.value: Canonicalize repeated-dot custom provider source identities
Regression in PR #42: repeated leading dot operands diverge from stored custom descriptors and affected silently skips changed evidence.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Read issue #43 in full via REST and inspected origin/main 049dc82. The custom branch of sourceIdentity strips one leading dot slash per call, unlike the idempotent built-in branch. Plan: canonicalize only leading dot prefixes for custom providers, preserve opaque suffixes and legacy persisted records, and verify raw operands, descriptor comparisons and adapter/cache reads through real gitless SDK trackers and the built package.

value.text: Failing-first proof on unchanged main 049dc82: node --test --test-concurrency=2 test/custom-source-paths.test.ts reports 0 pass, 3 fail. No stored citation rewrite and no dependency changes.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Re-review: PRRT_kwDOVUfUaM60xHMw is valid. General rule: operator-input normalization and refusal policy must depend on explicit configuration, never on stored records or enumeration order, and must finish before source reads. The current fallback accepts custom-only operands up front but lazily re-normalizes them for built-in citations; built-in-only traversal operands can likewise fail only after encountering a custom citation. Plan: compute both domain filters once before tracker enumeration, retain strict configured-custom traversal refusals, and explicitly report operands restricted to one provider domain in the public scope. Audit SDK, CLI, JSON/TOON, packed consumers and no-git tracker behavior; add corpus/order adversarial tests and a function-only revert proof. The prior fixes, commits and saved-WIP cleanup remain complete.

Replaced both late-domain failures with one preflight filter computed from explicit adapters. Custom-only operands are visibly restricted by scope.customOnlyChanged; built-in-only operands by scope.builtinOnlyChanged. Configured custom adapters still reject traversal, now before tracker enumeration and source reads. Fixed tests pass 2/2 across all 65 ordered corpora each, preserving native history, released legacy records and native JSON/TOON behavior.
